div.head: VII Atr 3.1
div.ab: Et ad singulas horas decantet totus conuentus extensis membris in terra psalmum illum: ‘Domine, quid multiplicati sunt’ et collectam contra paganos; et hoc fiat, quamdiu necessitas ista nobis est in manibus.

Et ad singulas horas decantet totus conventus extensis membris in terra psalmum illum: "Domine, quid multiplicati sunt," et collectam contra paganos; et hoc fiat quamdiu necessitas ista nobis est in manibus.

Et ad singulas horas decantet totus conventus extensis membris in terra psalmum illum: Domine, quid multiplicati sunt et collectam contra paganos; et hoc fiat, quamdiu necessitas ista nobis est in manibus.

Und zu den einzelnen Horen singe der ganze Convent, die Glieder auf der Erde ausgestreckt, den [dritten] Psalm: ‘Ach Herr, wie sind [meiner Feinde] so viel’ und die Collecte gegen die Heiden; und dies geschehe, so lange diese Noth vorhanden ist.

And at each of the hours let the whole community, lying prostrate on the ground, sing the [third] psalm, ‘Lord, how are they increased [that trouble me]’, and the collect against the heathen; and let this be done as long as this need is upon us.

And at the various Hours all the members of the foundation, prostrate on the ground, shall chant the psalm: "O Lord, how are they multiplied," and the Collect against the heathen, and this shall be done as long as the present need continues.

And at each of the canonical hours, all members of the community, lying on the ground with limbs extended, are to chant the psalm, Lord, how they are multiplied, and the Collect against the pagans; and this is to be done as long as we have the need.

Lord, how they are multiplied: Psalm 3.
Collect: A prayer, often used at the beginning of a service, to call the congregants together.

note.seg: Die Bittpsalmen vorzugsweise finden sich in den Hss. mit Agsächs. Glossen versehen, weil man sie gegen die Dänen sang; Wildhagen Studien z. Psalt. in Morsbach Festschr. 460. Der Homilet 171 setzt diese Vorschrift für verschiedene Notfälle und benennt den Psalm nicht

It is the psalms of supplication above all that are found furnished with Anglo-Saxon glosses in the MSS, because they were sung against the Danes; Wildhagen Studien z. Psalt. in Morsbach Festschr. 460. The homilist 171 prescribes this for various emergencies and does not name the psalm
